simple.meaning: מִמְשָׁל (mimshâl) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a ruler or (abstractly) rule.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Daniel, beginning at 2 Kings 20:13. The surrounding contexts include birth, family, family line, kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִמְשָׁל (H4474) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מִמְשָׁל (mimshâl) / H4474 is traced through 2 Kings 20:13, 1 Chronicles 26:6, 2 Chronicles 8:6, Daniel 11:3 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H4474. mimshal מִמְשָׁל noun [masculine] dominion, ruler (late); — absolute ׳מ Dan 11:3 , 5 ; plural הַמִּמְשָׁלִים 1Chr 26:6 ; — 1 ׳מ רב great dominion Dan 11:3 (accusative of congnate meaning with verb with מָשַׁל ), 11:5 (predicate of מֶמְשַׁלְתּוֺ ). 2 abstract for concrete (plural) = rulers 1Chr 26:6 (? read הַמּשְׁלִים ).

occurrences.englishText: Hezekiah listened to them, and showed them all the storehouse of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and the house of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. Sons were also born to Shemaiah his son, who ruled over the house of their father; for they were mighty men of valor.

and Baalath, and all the storage cities that Solomon had, and all the cities for his chariots, the cities for his horsemen, and all that Solomon desired to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.
A mighty king will stand up, who will rule with great dominion, and do according to his will.
